reviews.text: It has only been a couple of weeks and I am already seeing huge progress in my furry friend’s behavior. The staff is so friendly and meets your every need. They listen to questions and is always happy to answer any question I might have! Koda gets excited to see them every time. They put the dogs safety first and is so caring. I would recommend sit means sit to anyone!! Definitely worth it!!

I can’t recommend this place enough. My dog Odin was terrible with leash walking and bad reactivity when he’s outside. The training and teaching has been amazing and beneficial. They really want you and your dog to be successful. It’s been amazing working with them.

Love that the group classes are included as part of the program we chose.  I had little experience with training and being able to go back to reinforce all the things my dog had learned with guidance from the trainers is so helpful.

I just wanted to drop a quick review:  Bastogne and I have been going to class for quite a while now.  We are both getting better but much work to be done.  At the end of class today I sat down and played with Chewy while Kendall kept Bastogne.  She did a few drills with him while I sat there. Bastogne was actually doing pretty well with the drills which was good to see but what really struck me was the absolute joy he was experiencing working with her.  He had had a long day but you could plainly see his delight in working with his trainer. He was having a blast.  When I tell people about Sit Means Sit I could talk about the curriculum and tools but that is almost meaningless compared to the people.  Dogs don't know about faking it. They are happy or they are not. He loves his trainers and that makes me so very happy. He actually got a little too excited and had a bit of the zoomies but I will take a happy dog every day. Thanks to everyone who has made such a difference on our journey and today a special thanks to Kendall for giving me such a great memory-- one where I could simply watch Bastogne having a great day.  Also thanks for letting me play with Chewy.

I took my puppy who is a Boston terrier to Sit Means Sit when she was five months old. Even at her young age, they were very patient with her and she responded very well and is now a well-behaved, disciplined puppy. Kendall was her favorite trainer and did a great job with her!

We love Sit Means Sit! This program and the wonderful trainers have changed our life & our dynamic with our reactive dog for the better. My husband and I have learned the tools to set our dog and us up for success. We have elected to continue taking the group classes and I see improvement every class in our best boy! Kendall sets up challenges for the dogs to work their skills but also for the dog parents too. We cannot recommend sit means sit enough.. Ask for Kendall!
Did the hybrid training for a reactive dog. Still early, but really happy with the results so far and looking forward to the 6 months of group classes.

We’ve had a great experience throughout our pup’s training program. Kendall and the rest of the team are very accommodating and have been super helpful with addressing our pup’s impulse control and recall. Would recommend!
Great dog training services, staff is always super friendly and helpful! Damian and Kendall are amazing and always willing to help out with any questions. Highly recommend!
Kendall is the BEST trainer! Our dog Bori has improved drastically after being trained by her and we’re super happy with our classes here :)

Five stars, without hesitation.

We sent our 9-month old pit bull to Sit Means Sit, and the experience exceeded what I hoped for. Morgan and her co-trainer (whose name I regrettably can’t recall) were particularly incredible, and the entire team made the process feel personal from beginning to end. They were flexible, responsive, and just as invested in helping us succeed once our girl came home as they were in training her while she was there.

What really made Sit Means Sit worth it for us was that they weren’t just training our dog. They were training our whole family.

There are certainly less expensive places where you can send a dog away for two weeks of training, but I wanted something that would actually last. With Sit Means Sit, the board-and-train was really the foundation. I love that they then transitioned us to 6 months of continued training so we could learn how to be better handlers, reinforce what our girl had learned, and keep her from going back to all of her old habits.

And when we picked her up, she was so excited to see us that she was basically operating at a 20 out of 10. The trainers warned us that she might act like she had forgotten everything because it was the happiest day of her life. 😂 But we followed their instructions, stayed consistent, and watched everything click into place.

The difference at home has been amazing. Before training, it sometimes felt like managing puppy chaos was taking over our lives. We were constantly chasing her through the house, worrying about her getting away from us, redirecting behavior, and trying to figure out what to do next. It was exhausting, and honestly, it was starting to affect our relationship with her.

What I love most is that she’s still her energetic, funny, loving, and very puppy self, but there’s structure. She understands what we are asking of her, and we understand how to communicate with her. Our home is calmer, she seems happier, and instead of spending all of our energy managing her behavior, we can focus on loving her the way she deserves to be loved.

We couldn’t be happier with the personalized experience and value for our investment. I’m incredibly grateful to Morgan and the entire training team!

My pups love, love Ms Kendall!  You can tell she is absolutely a dog lover to her core.  My babies have responded so well with her and we have been able to be so much better neighborhood dogs. If you want to have well behaved puppers and be able to take them out in public with confidence, bring them here!

Eva May, my awesome Lagotto Romagnolo puppy (aka truffle dog), has been part of the Sit Means Sit (SMS) family since she was 14 weeks old, and in about 10 weeks, the growth I've seen in her has been remarkable. She's now an AKC S.T.A.R. Puppy, a Hybrid Training graduate, and at just under six months old, she's already developed enough skills and confidence to train in the Intermediate Group alongside full-grown dogs! But it didn’t happen overnight or by accident. Eva’s success reflects an enormous amount of time, consistency, patience, and genuine care from Robert, Damien, Kendall, Austin, and Lisa. Every one of them has contributed something meaningful to Eva’s development.

I especially want to recognize Kendall and Damien, who have poured an extraordinary amount of time, energy, and love into working with Eva May. I have watched them challenge her, encourage her, praise her progress, and genuinely enjoy who she is as a puppy. That matters tremendously to me. I can see how much those relationships mean to Eva when her tail starts wagging as we pull up and she rushes inside to greet everyone. Austin has always been incredibly helpful and engaged as the manager; Lisa (the owner) is hands-on, working one-on-one with Eva, and has created an environment where both dogs and their people are supported, empowered, and encouraged to grow together; Robert has also been an important part of Eva’s training journey, especially during our early-morning drop-offs. What I value most is knowing how much this team genuinely loves Eva. I pay very close attention to the people I trust with my pup, and because I can see the relationships they've each built with Eva, I have complete confidence that SMS will always do right by her when I walk out the door.

At this point, SMS is more than just somewhere Eva goes for training. This team has become part of the talented and loving ecosystem surrounding her as she grows up. She's their first Lagotto Romagnolo, and I can tell they took the time to study her breed. They know her, care about her, celebrate her, and continue to help me bring out the very best in her.

I'm incredibly proud of the dog Eva May is becoming, and SMS deserves a great deal of credit for helping her get there. We are grateful to have them in her life and look forward to sharing many more milestones and memories with everyone at SMS as Eva grows.

I sent my 3 year old reactive doberman to the boarding classes, and attended the six months of group classes after, and here are my thoughts:
If your dog has true behavioral issues, your money is better off spent with a 1-on-1 trainer. I am a broke college student and I regret that I spent the equivalent of a semester's tuition here since my dog has many of the same issues as before in the real world- yes, she can do what's expected of her in the group classes, and now I have a tool that can sort of get her attention if I catch her in time before a reaction, but the advice given there is very general when she would have benefited much more from a 1 on 1 approach to address the underlying issues. My dog was already obedient, and that's most of what was worked on in class, and while her reactivity could be managed in that very controlled setting it was difficult to translate to real world scenarios. Its partly my fault for not being able to show up to all of of the classes due to work/school; however, I felt that even when I did get a day off to attend, she would do well in class but I didn't gain the knowledge or experience that would truly help me avoid reactions on our walks/hikes. Both I and my dog needed more specific training to our scenario, which I could have gotten for the same price elsewhere. But again- the group environment might work very well for your dog if that is not the issue. I have seen very well behaved dogs there, so this is just to speak for my specific situation.
I want to emphasize that I appreciate the tips and support that I was provided by the facility- it just wasn't the best approach for our situation. I feel sorry to write that I didn't have the best results because the staff is very friendly and they do well at polishing up your dog's obedience. But honestly, in my own opinion if you are looking for a solution for your dog's difficult behavior such as dog reactivity, your money would be better spent with a more individualized approach.

I wanted to give an honest review of my experience with Sit Means Sit. I did a two-week board-and-train with my puppy back in June, paying nearly $4,000. I went into it with several specific goals: improving her recall so she could eventually be off leash, stopping her from picking on our older dog, getting her to stop biting the leash, improving her leash manners, teaching her not to jump all over people when she gets excited, and teaching basic boundaries like not running out the door or chasing after people.

Unfortunately, I honestly don’t feel like she learned the things we paid for. She still has extremely poor recall, gets overly excited when she sees people, wants to chase/play with every dog or cat she sees, and still struggles with basic obedience and boundaries.

The program also included training sessions where we were taught how to continue her training at home. They use an e-collar, which I wasn’t very educated about beforehand. During one of our sessions, the trainer instructed me to press the button every time I turned or changed direction while walking. I didn’t understand why that was necessary when my puppy was already following me, and looking back, I wish I had questioned it more.

After the board-and-train, I waited about a month before reaching back out because I wanted to give her time and genuinely hoped things would improve. I was told that if she needed additional training, they would work with her at no additional cost. However, I was ultimately directed toward group classes.

The problem is that my puppy simply isn’t ready for a group class. She becomes extremely distracted and excited around other dogs and cats and wants to get to them to play. Even during our training sessions, she struggled to listen, and I was told that she was a puppy and was tired. I live in Kerrville, so making repeated trips for group classes is also difficult, especially when I don’t believe she’s at the point where a group environment would be productive for her.

Another major disappointment was the lack of follow-up after her training. I expected someone from the facility to check in and ask how things were going, especially after spending nearly $4,000 on her training. I never heard one word from them. Every time there was communication afterward, I was the one who had to reach out and explain that we were still struggling. I feel like there should have been more follow-up and support instead of leaving it up to me to keep contacting them.

I truly wanted this to work, and I gave it time before saying anything. But for nearly $4,000, I expected much more progress and individualized follow-up when the training clearly wasn’t accomplishing what we discussed beforehand.

I don’t expect every puppy to be perfect after two weeks, but I did expect to see meaningful progress and continued support afterward. Unfortunately, that wasn’t my experience.

Based on my personal experience, I would not recommend this location for a puppy with the issues mine had. If you’re considering spending this kind of money on training, I would strongly encourage you to research other trainers and ask very detailed questions about exactly what methods will be used, what progress you should realistically expect, and what happens if your dog doesn’t meet the training goals.

Our sweet Lab, Gracie Mae, absolutely loved the staff at Sit Means Sit! She was incredibly responsive to her new commands, and after just two weeks of summer camp, she came home like a completely different dog—in the best way!

It’s so nice having her wait patiently for me to go through the door first, and “place” has a whole new meaning in our house now! The difference in her manners, responsiveness, and confidence has been amazing.

The training at Sit Means Sit is truly top-notch, and we couldn’t be happier with our experience. We highly recommend them for any breed, any age, and any training need. Thank you for taking such wonderful care of our Gracie Mae and giving us the tools to continue her training at home! 🐾❤️

Everyone here is great and Enzo has learned so much .  We love all the trainers and Kendal has been great during the classes and the boarding they offer as well. We also love the app they have to keep track of progress.

We brought our mastiff girl to Sit Means Sit in the hopes of helping to be a more social and well behaved dog.
We brought our Rottie to them years ago and he is well trained and balanced.
From the setup to the lessons all team members were friendly, informative and professional.
Training was setup by Austin with a few date adjustments he was happy to accommodate.
We were always greeted by Scott in a friendly way upon drop off.
Robert would take her out for a walk first thing, I mentioned to him she was leery of the guys out in the parking lot from a neighboring business and he made a point of walking her around them to help desensitize her.
Kendall was her trainer, Maze loves her which is big for her as she has bad “stranger danger” fears.
Kendall is awesome with her, helping her work through her fears and obedience issues.
I’m looking forward to on going group classes which should keep her growing and meeting more people.
Highly recommended!

The dog trainers were excellent…very dedicated and professional. They genuinely cared for our dog, Sophie and they made sure they addressed all of our concerns.
Our dog loved working with Morgan.🌻

If I could give 10 ⭐️ I absolutely would! I knew my Roxy needed training but really I did! @Kendall has been so amazing to us and taught us so much. Every training session she makes me and Roxy comfortable and I love how she loves my fluffy Roxy girl too! Since we started coming to train with Kendall, I’ve been able to take Roxy on a 5K, to a work conference, restaurants and really anywhere I go! Her anxiety is better and so is mine!

We’re genuinely grateful that Sit Means Sit was able to help us out when we needed boarding for our puppy. The staff was kind, and we appreciated having a safe place for her to stay.

That said, our experience with the actual training side of the program was disappointing. After two weeks, our puppy did not come home with any noticeable improvement in her basic commands. She didn’t respond to “come,” “place,” “drop it,” “leave it,” or “quiet,” and her impulse control seems mostly unchanged. Her leash walking is essentially the same as it was before we brought her in.

From what we observed, the primary method used to get results at the facility appears to be the e-collar. She was terrified and traumatized by the collar. Other training approaches were minimal at best, and we didn’t see evidence of a broader or balanced training plan. Considering the amount of time she spent there, we expected her to at least have a basic understanding of the foundational commands we were told she would learn—but that simply didn’t happen.

We appreciate the kindness of the staff, but the training outcomes did not meet our expectations.

Sit Means Sit taught us the skills necessary to keep our mini Australian Shepherd puppy active and happy in a controlled way. These herding breeds need a job in the home… even if it means patiently sitting in place.  The instructors were encouraging, motivating and professional. The training took intentionality and time, but it was well worth the investment so that we could enjoy our dog and so could family, and friends that came into contact with her. We highly recommend their services!
So happy to have found Sit means Sit. The trainer has been awesome in teaching me and my dog. I highly recommend checking them out.

10/10 recommended! I went to their cibolo location for a board and train program and was extremely happy with my results. They are very hands on and provide all the tips and tricks to upkeep training. Give them a call!

When Noah adopted us after being on the streets for so long that he was going to need training . We began looking for a training environment that would be suitable for him . There are multiple businesses available for dog training with different approaches. We still needed more information so a visit was necessary. Noah entered the in boarding program which lasted two weeks with home visits on the weekends. After the initial training process we are seeing a trained gentleman giant and takes commands comfortably. Noah and I take advantage of the evening training sessions enjoying observing his continued progress . I would recommend Sit Means Sit to anyone in need of training for their pet

The Sit Means Sit-Broadway location has been absolutely amazing with training my dog Buddy. Buddy is a very sweet dog but was very reactive when seeing other dogs on walks. After the very 1st private session, I noticed a small positive change in Buddy's behavior. After the 3rd session, the change was remarkable! After our 4th session next week, Buddy and I will be participating in group classes and pack walks. Buddy looks forward to going to his classes and loves his trainers, particularly Kendall who has gone above and beyond for my doggie! Sit Means Sit has payment plans that are affordable and reasonable, and the facility is exceptionally clean and doesn't smell like dog! Austin the operations manager and his staff are always friendly and accommodating. It's clear they love what they do! 5 Stars!!!
This experience has been amazing. I now love taking Nova out in public. We have also really enjoyed our group classes and pack walks. Thank you 😊
Best place ever for max. He was dog reactive and now he is as calm as a cucumber

I went training today with Josh today.  He is very involved with each pet and pet owner. He had all of us giving our pets commands, near the end he realized how tired most were so he changed it to having them sit and us doing crazy things to break the command. IT TOTALLY RE-ENGAGED! My dog got more alert and showed energy.  Great training today!!

Absolutely love this place because my dog loves it too! My dog, Fudge, is always excited to come train at this facility. Every time we arrive, he immediately starts wagging his tail and gets excited to see all the handlers who trained him during his two-week course. It makes me happy seeing how excited he is to come here because I know that means he’s treated well.

The handlers are awesome, and they always provide great communication and guidance whenever I need it. I would definitely recommend this place to anyone who needs help with their pup!

Let me start by saying I am a true dog lover and my husband is not.  So when we decided to get a rescue it would be on me to train him.   My husband was frustrated with my lack of progress.  I decided I needed help.  My trainer was supportive and loving and just amazing.   I have the best well behaved dog and it was all because Isit means sit.  Not to be too dramatic but it saved my marriage by having a happy well behaved dog.  Thank you Kendall.  She is a dream to work with.

We are so thankful that we finally decided to enroll our dog with Sit Means Sit Dog Training! Our dog has always been super smart and interested in learning, but S.M.S.D.T gave her and us a stronger  foundation that she deserves. The entire staff is so awesome, but we had a very focused experience with Josh and can't thank him enough for his patience and expertise with Bijou. You guys rock! Thank you!

We love Josh at sit means sit! Our dog olive is very bratty and Josh has helped immensely with her behavior. Josh is even a kid whisperer and gets my kids to understand how to help train olive. Olive is still a work in progress but we wouldn’t be where we are without Josh. We are so thankful we found Josh at sit means sit.

We had a wonderful experience with Sit Means Sit.  Everyone was so nice. Our trainer Josh was especially great to work with.  He was very patient with us and very informative.  We really appreciated the extra time he took with us during our lesson.  Also the way he explained our dogs behavior and responses in a way we could relate to.  Would absolutely recommend.
Josh did an excellent job in helping our 7 month old dog named Cashew learn manners and skills. We recommend anyone interested in training your dog to go here!

Sit Means Sit has been a very rewarding and fantastic experience  in the board-and-train program for my dog Ellie!. Recently, I discovered Sit Means Sit, and they have been very loving and attentive to her training and helping me with Ellie's learning.  She loves going to the classes and the boarding program.  They send pictures and updates, recognizing her excited interest in learning and her genuine care for people.   She  arrived home wanting to learn more, and happy about showing me what she learns; she gets excited for our walks and our hikes like never before.  Ellie recognizes what she needs to do. The trainers at Sit Means Sit are kind, knowledgeable, patient, and they take great care to help me learn as well. They care deeply about the relationship between Ellie and me, and leaving Ellie with the trainers feels like another home.  The follow-up training sessions explore even more ways for us to get better together.  I highly recommend this caring business.  They are loving and diligent in their attention to the training Ellie needs as she learns and grows, and also how I can become a better caretaker for Ellie.  I cant say enough about our experience.

We can’t say enough good things about the team at Sit Means Sit. From day one, they’ve been knowledgeable, encouraging, and genuinely invested in our dog’s success.
Our pup loves going to class — he actually knows he’s headed to “school” when we turn right out of our neighborhood! We’re so happy with the progress our boy has made. The growth in his focus, responsiveness, and confidence has been amazing to see. We’re incredibly grateful for the time and care the Sit Means Sit team has poured into him!

Nemo has attended the All Star Puppy class and also the hybrid board & training. He also does the enrichment classes once a week. Nemo is very impulsive and needs very structured training. Sit means Sit has done a phenomenal job in training Nemo. The staff is very knowledgeable and supportive in training me to work with him at home.

Reading some of the negative reviews about e-collars can definitely be intimidating, but not every training method is right for every dog—and that’s exactly why I’m so glad we chose this place. We brought both of our dogs in for a consultation with Austin, and instead of pushing us into an expensive “both dogs need board-and-train” situation like other places did, he was completely honest. He recommended that only our boy needed the hybrid board-and-train and that we could use what we learned with him to help our girl at home. That alone showed us they weren’t just in it for a quick money grab.

Yes, the price is on the higher side, but when you actually break it down, the value is incredible. The package is $3,150, and it includes six months of group classes for free after the two-week hybrid board-and-train. There is also payment plan options. Over those two weeks, your dog is working with trainers five days a week, eight hours a day. When you divide the cost, it comes out to about $39 an hour—and that’s without using the 6 months of free classes. Other training programs I looked into were charging $100+ an hour. So while the upfront price is steep, you truly get what you pay for.

One thing I really appreciated is that they send photos and videos every single day, which made it so much easier being away from our boy and let us see his progress in real time.

Drop-off was Monday and pick-up was Friday both weeks, and after each week we had a training session with Kendall. She was absolutely amazing—so patient, knowledgeable, and genuinely treated our boy like her own. Now that we’ve started the skills-and-drills group classes with Josh, I’m even happier with our decision. Our first class was tough because our boy can be reactive, but Josh stayed patient, calm, and incredibly helpful. By the second class, it was a complete night-and-day difference.

I honestly couldn’t recommend this training team more. They care, they’re transparent, and they deliver real results.
Great service. Great communication
Hi Debora. I have looked in our database and don’t see you in our system.  We stand behind our work 100%. Please give me a call 210-414-2788.

I was moving from a house with a yard to an apartment.  My dog was afraid of other dogs and was prone to aggressive barking, pulling on the leash and lunging.  Sit Means Sit was able to make her comfortable around other dogs and provide the advanced leash skills necessary for apartment living.  (Most importantly, they also provided me with owner training.) When she refused the elevator after our move they provided additional follow up training.

There are many dog trainers being advertised.  Sit means Sit sticks out of the crowd for their superior training expertise.
Great place and my little girl is learning a lot and she seems like she is having fun. Absolutely love this place. I couldn't be more happy with our decision to come to Sit Means Sit.

General ( Bulldog ) experience is 💯 % above  standard . If I had to pick one word to describe both my furry pet & my experience in the 3 week Board and train . Exceptional. From customer service to employees . I don’t do reviews but this company deserves the praise . Thank you from the bottom of my heart . Best Trainers in San Antonio .

Josh, Kendall, and the rest of the staff  have been absolutely fantastic with our dog Pickles. Their training has brought tremendous improvements in his impulse control and overall behavior, and we couldn’t be happier with the results. I’m excited to see his continued progress and look forward to participating in the upcoming all-call group class.

Omar & Pickles

We first brought our special-needs Yorkie to Sit Means Sit for one-on-one training. At just 4 pounds, she was our tiny little girl, and the team treated her with the same care and love we do. She came home a completely transformed puppy.

When we added a new 4-month-old Yorkie to our family, we returned to Sit Means Sit for his initial training and will begin one-on-one sessions soon. Every trainer there treats your pups with the same affection and respect you would—they truly care for your babies like their own.

Sit Means Sit has consistently gone above and beyond to care for us and our little Beau. As first-time dog owners, we were unsure how to navigate dog training and finding the right support. We shopped around but immediately felt at home with the team at Sit Means Sit. Austin has personally given so much of his time to offer us advice as challenges come up. We’ve done the AKC Star Puppy Class and we’re now looking into doing the adult dog training program with them.

We started training with our dog Beans when he was just 8 months old, and the improvement has been incredible—truly a night and day difference. As first-time dog owners, we were going in completely blind and had no idea where to begin. Josh has been a game-changer. He not only taught us effective training techniques, but also helped us understand how a dog thinks, which gave us a whole new perspective on Beans and his behavior. There's still a lot to learn, but we're feeling confident and excited for the journey ahead. Highly recommend!

The team at Sit Means Sit (Cibolo) is very patient and understanding while training my dog (and me).  Before, my dog was unruly and would drag me on his walks but now he is better behaved.  He still has room to improve but we have a few more months of group sessions to help reenforce the commands and better behavior.  I especially like the advice and techniques taught by Taz; she has been a terrific help.

We took our dog, Bruno, a king shepherd dog, to the Cibolo facility for board and train. He was experiencing fear aggression toward strangers, and it seemed to be getting worse. We were worrying about what could happen if it progressed further. Our vet recommended Sit Means Sit. Bruno can now sit in place and not bark when a friend or family member who is a stranger to him comes over. He can also walk with a loose leash. We are continuing with his training at home, and he is doing great. Everyone at the facility was very helpful. I got pictures and updates every day on his progress. After a few days, he seemed like he was having fun with his training. Taz was his primary trainer, and Sawyer was also helpful. Many thanks to Austin, Taz, and Sawyer. Bruno has come a long way!

Recently took the AKC Star Puppy class and it was the best puppy class! Trainers were wonderful and taught us so much. Highly recommend still!

My dog loves going to training at Sit Means Sit. We have so much fun every time we attend a class. My dog was initially fear aggressive towards other dogs but after a week of board and train with Karis and consistently attending classes she is almost normal when in close proximity of other dogs. I would highly recommend Sit Means Sit San Antonio due to the high quality of trainers who are knowledgeable professionals.

I was a little worried about the money, but it’s worth every penny. The whole staff did a great job with our dog Buck. Thanks for all the hard work that you guys do. And I just want to thank Josh specifically just because he was the one we interacted w the most. Josh is super cool and easy going when it comes to explaining the drills. And appreciate the whole staff but especially my boy Josh! Really enjoying the skills and drills w him as well and our dog is getting better each week. With patience and practice it gets easier!

We brought home two 11 week old yorkies in January and immediately began to panic. They were sweet and loving babies, but we were overwhelmed! After speaking with several local trainers, Sit Means Sit came to our rescue. Austin, Lisa and Josh made time for several one-on-one sessions with us, came to our home and gave us much needed encouragement and support. At 16 weeks the girls started 3 weeks of boarding training with weekends at home. They worked hard and thrived with the instruction they received. They loved their time at SMS and all the staff that interacted with them. We have been following-up with group training classes and the girls have recently graduated to the intermediate level! We want to commend SMS for their professionalism, knowledge and loving care of Mia and Miki – and us! If you choose this team you are in great hands. Thank you, SMS!

I have really been enjoying Sit means Sit! The staff is so nice and friendly and took care of my boys so carefully, which I really appreciated. Both of my dogs have gotten through the hybrid onboarding which I’m also so grateful they had this option. My older dog is 4 and although he’s stubborn, I’ve seen a lot of improvement in him, in just a matter of weeks. I also have really enjoyed getting to work with Josh during my training lessons for both my boys! He is very knowledgeable and he’s been great at teaching and explaining everything along the way.

Well our fur boy Herschel just graduated from SMS. We have loved the experience, the goal and the learning. All the trainers have been joy and our boy loved going to work and learn.

The experience was one of a kind and if you’re looking for great people that really care about your dog then don’t think twice and sign up with SMS.

We completed puppy class and moved on to the board/train class. The immersive training completed in these classes is by far the best but the best part is the trainers and their love and passion for dogs. The app and communication from SMS daily will keep you in touch with your fur baby.

If you have questions and concerns about the program they will sit down with you via phone or in person and walk you through the program and techniques.

Hands down the best!!!

Austin, Josh, Caitlyn, Kendall and Scott you guys all are the best. Thank you for all your help, patience and mostly safe keeping of our fur baby!

Bull terriers are known for being stubborn and definitely have a mind of their own. Sit Means Sit has helped us and Ria tremendously in being able to get a handle on some of her quirky personality traits. Ria adores all of the trainers, as do we!! We love taking Ria out in public and they have helped us establish commands and manners for when we do. Not to mention other basic commands we use at home and around the neighborhood. Cannot recommended them highly enough!

I wanted to take just a minute to share a review of the great team at Sit Means Sit of San Antonio. Our dog, JD, a 3.5 yr old male German Shepherd and myself, have been working with Kendall and Josh at the Broadway location since early September.

The development and improvement that JD has achieved since Sept '24 has absolutely amazed us. He started out with both Dog and People Aggression and has pretty much left all of that behind him now after attending weekly classes and learning to work thru those things. Wish there was a lower rating to assign to this facility. Took my dog there for multiple day long sessions as a refresher obedience. He had already passed his CGC so didn’t need much training. Found out he wasn’t fed (I took his lunch every day). They told me they turned up the shock collar to a 6 out of 10, but initially said they never do that. How I regret taking him there. The same day, he bit the trainer in my presence. She said she couldn’t work with him after being bitten, so handed me a muzzle to put on him which was added to my bill. That night my dog became aggressive toward me. The trainer emailed me to say this is normal and I need to demonstrate that I wasn’t afraid of him. Wish they’d told me that during the introductory meeting. I’d have left. Seems they use a one size fits all training. The e-collar (aka negative reinforcement) doesn’t work for all dogs. I removed him from the program immediately.

The fear free trainer that I know had warned me that my dog could become aggressive if the e-collar were used. Well it happened. Less than a year later, I had to destroy my dog as he had become aggressive toward me. This was a dog that I used to take out in public and had no fear, that walked calmly through a thick crowd, enjoyed doggy daycare. I blame myself every day for making this choice. I am now very careful about the training environment in which I place my dogs. I will never use this facility or any other facility that uses similar methods again.
